topic.angle: The phone book of the internet

body.claim: When you type a website name, a system called DNS looks up its numeric address for you.
body.why: Computers find each other by IP addresses, which are numbers like 192.0.2.172. DNS uses special servers to match a name you can remember, like mozilla.org, to the real address. Large sites run on multiple servers, so the address you get may vary depending on where you are.

probes.question: What does DNS do?
options: Turns a website name into an IP address

probes.question: True or false: a website's IP address may vary depending on where you are.

claims.claim: DNS looks up a numeric address for a website name
claims.quote: special servers that match up a web address you type into your browser

claims.claim: Computers use IP addresses that are numbers like 192.0.2.172
claims.quote: special numbers that look like this: 192.0.2.172

claims.claim: Title: DNS is the internet's phone book
claims.quote: serves as the phone book for the Internet by translating human-friendly computer hostnames into IP addresses

claims.claim: Large sites run on multiple servers
claims.quote: Large websites are commonly made available on multiple servers, so that they load efficiently for different users worldwide.

claims.claim: The IP address may vary depending on where you are (probe 2: true)
claims.quote: As a result, the IP address may vary depending on where you are.
